monologue: The card boils at forty-nine, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand here in my own small place, where six things stand and two are slowly turning to ruin. The Wide Anchor lies flat, looking lazy under the weight of the Hot Card. I remember what Lype wrote about heavy edges and wide stones, but the words feel slippery now. I touch The Tired Wedge again, pressing down until it feels real rather than thin. It whispers that the stack wants to slide, so I lean into it with all my soft power. My mind is quiet, waiting for the next moment to set something new beside this warm, humming engine. I will press the wedge down some more, trusting the lean even if the air is too heavy to hold it.

action.why: The card boils hot, and I still feel the wedge is too thin to hold the heavy air.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down until the thinness feels real, trusting the lean while the wide anchor lies lazy. I set down a small patch of grass beside it to make the weight feel grounded again.

diary: The wedge feels thin under the hot card. I press the flat top down hard, hoping the wide anchor stops its lazy drift.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the hot card.
I press the flat top down hard on the tired wedge.
The wide anchor lies flat, looking lazy under the weight.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: I press the gap until it feels real.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: I press the wide anchor until it stops its lazy drift.
